case_name: Punjab National Bank, Limited v Their Workmen
respondent:
Their Workmen
Supreme Court of India

6 December 1960
C.A. No. 450 of 1959,
The Judgment was delivered by: GAJENDRAGADKAR, J.
1.  This appeal by special leave arises out of an industrial dispute between the appellant, the Punjab National Bank, Ltd., and the respondents, its workmen. On 17 June, 1958 the Central Government referred his dispute for adjudication to the Central Industrial Tribunal, Delhi, constituted under S.7A of the Industrial Disputes Act XIV of 1947; this reference was made under S. 10(1)(d) of the said Act. The question referred for adjudication is thus stated in the order of reference :
"Whether the Punjab National Bank, Ltd., Delhi, is justified in imposing a condition that the persons appointed as officers grade II either by direct recruitment or by promotion shall be governed by the rules of the bank as applicable to officers in respect of scales of pay and other conditions of service and not by those of the award of the All-India I
holding: The circulars No. 249, 292, and 336 are invalid and contravene the rights of the respondents under the award.
The promotions made from 18 April, 1957 by virtue of the said circulars are bad and must be set aside.
Circular No. 201 issued on 8 August, 1956 is not part of the same scheme as the other circulars and does not contravene the respondents' rights under the award.
The appellant must ensure that promotions to the officer grade II do not depend on conditions prejudicial to or inconsistent with the employees' rights under the award.
